bullets.title: Advanced Paediatric Assessment and Prioritisation
bullets.text: International paediatric practice expects nurses to combine structured assessment with developmental knowledge and clinical judgement. Children can compensate until late in illness, so subtle trends and caregiver concerns must be taken seriously.

bullets.title: Managing High-Risk Paediatric Conditions
bullets.text: High-risk paediatric conditions can deteriorate rapidly. Nurses must anticipate complications, deliver age-appropriate interventions and coordinate care with specialist teams.

bullets.title: Complex Medication, Chronic Illness and Discharge Care
bullets.text: Children with chronic or complex conditions may rely on multiple medicines, devices and caregivers. Safe care requires precise calculation, education and coordination across hospital, school and community settings.

bullets.title: Safeguarding, Communication and Culturally Safe Care
bullets.text: International paediatric nurses must uphold children's rights, recognise safeguarding concerns and communicate in ways that respect culture, family structure and the child's developing autonomy.
